items.title: Fréchet spaces used in analytic coherent cohomology
items.statement:
A **Fréchet space** over $\mathbb C$ is a complex vector space $E$ with a Hausdorff locally convex vector-space topology generated by a separating countable family of seminorms $(p_n)_{n\ge1}$ and complete for its seminorm uniformity. Explicitly, use the translation-invariant compatible metric
$$d(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}\min\{1,p_n(x-y)\},$$
and require that this metric is complete. A seminorm is a function $p:E\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $p(x+y)\le p(x)+p(y)$ and $p(cx)=|c|p(x)$ for $x,y\in E$ and $c\in\mathbb C$; separating means that for $x\ne0$ some $p_n(x)>0$. Locally convex means that every point has a neighborhood basis of convex sets. One may replace the defining family by the increasing family of its finite maxima.

Completeness here always refers to this vector-space uniformity. A sequence is Cauchy for the displayed metric exactly when it is Cauchy for every defining seminorm: each individual metric summand controls that seminorm at sufficiently small distances, and conversely the geometric tail of the metric series plus finitely many seminorm estimates controls the metric. Thus a seminorm-Cauchy series used in the accompanying proofs converges in $E$. The zero vector space is included, with its unique metric. This is the usual complete metrizable locally convex Fréchet convention.
items.axiom_base: ZF; definition only, with no choice operation and no physical premise.

items.title: Presentation and Čech quotient topologies for coherent analytic sections
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaf. On an open set $V$ contained in a coordinate chart and in a neighborhood with a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$, where $p_0,p_1$ are finite nonnegative ranks, require that the section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Give $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ the compact-convergence topology generated by the seminorms $f\mapsto\sup_{z\in K}\lVert f(z)\rVert$ for compact $K\subset V$, and give $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ the quotient topology induced by that surjection. On any open subset covered by countably many such sets, use the topology of the closed subspace of the product of their local section spaces consisting of compatible families. For a finite ordered open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ whose nonempty finite intersections have these section topologies, give each Čech cochain space

$$C^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_q}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_q},\mathcal F),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{q+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{q+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{q+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{q+1}}}.$$

the finite-product topology, give its cocycle space the subspace topology, and give the quotient of cocycles by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. The accompanying Fréchet-quotient lemma proves local chart and presentation independence; the compact projective-space finiteness theorem proves independence of its admissible finite acyclic cover topology.
items.axiom_base: ZF; definition only, conditional on the stated section-map surjections; no physical premise.

items.title: Baire category theorem for complete metric spaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space. If $X=\bigcup_{n\ge1}F_n$ for closed subsets $F_n\subseteq X$, then at least one $F_n$ has nonempty interior in $X$.

items.title: Open mapping theorem for Fréchet spaces
items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ and $F$ be Fréchet spaces over $\mathbb C$ and let $T:E\to F$ be a continuous, surjective, complex-linear map. Then $T$ is open: it sends every open subset of $E$ to an open subset of $F$.

items.title: Schwartz compact-perturbation theorem for Fréchet spaces
items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ and $F$ be Fréchet spaces over $\mathbb C$. A continuous linear map $g:E\to F$ is called a quasi-epimorphism when its image is closed and has finite codimension in $F$. A continuous linear map $h:E\to F$ is called compact when the image of some neighborhood of $0$ has compact closure in $F$. If $g$ is a quasi-epimorphism and $h$ is compact, then $g+h:E\to F$ is a quasi-epimorphism.
items.strategy: Finite-dimensional quotient reduction and controlled successive approximation prove the compact perturbation claim.

items.title: Compact morphisms of Fréchet complexes have finite Hausdorff cohomology
items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $(E^\bullet,d)$ and $(F^\bullet,\delta)$ be cochain complexes of Fréchet spaces over $\mathbb C$, with continuous differentials, and let $\rho^\bullet:E^\bullet\to F^\bullet$ be a continuous cochain map. Fix $q\ge0$. If $\rho^q:E^q\to F^q$ is compact and the induced map $H^q(\rho^\bullet):H^q(E^\bullet)\to H^q(F^\bullet)$ is surjective, then $H^q(F^\bullet)$, with its cocycle-subspace and coboundary-quotient topology, is Hausdorff and finite-dimensional. Moreover, whenever a continuous cochain map between Fréchet complexes induces a surjection on $q$th cohomology, that cohomology map is open.
items.strategy: Apply the compact perturbation theorem to cocycles plus coboundaries; prove openness of surjective cohomology maps.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be a Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain. Let $\mathcal O_\Omega$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. Then the derived sheaf cohomology satisfies $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal O_\Omega)=0$ for every integer $q>0$.

items.title: Coherent sheaves are acyclic on pseudoconvex intersections with local resolutions
items.statement: Assume full AC and the local Oka interface stated below. Let $r\ge1$, let $M$ be a complex manifold of complex dimension $r$, and let $V$ be an open subset of $M$ on which a coherent analytic module $\mathcal F$ is defined. Let $D_1,\ldots,D_s$ be relatively compact coordinate polydiscs in $M$ with nonempty intersection $V=\bigcap_{i=1}^sD_i$. Suppose that for one index $i_0$, a neighborhood of $\overline{D_{i_0}}$ in its chart lies in the domain of $\mathcal F$ and carries an exact partial finite-rank free resolution of $\mathcal F$ of length $2r$. Then $H^q(V,\mathcal F|_V)=0$ for every $q>0$. The result applies to a disconnected $V$ componentwise. The assumed local Oka interface is: under AC, on every finite-dimensional complex manifold $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent, coherent modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and finite extensions, and for each coherent $\mathcal F$, point $x$ and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, an exact partial finite-rank resolution $\mathcal O^{p_\ell}\to\cdots\to\mathcal O^{p_0}\to\mathcal F\to0$ exists on a chart neighborhood, exact at the module and all free terms except possibly the leftmost. No global free resolution is asserted.
items.strategy: Prove a psh exhaustion on chart intersections, then scalar acyclicity and conditional Oka dimension shifting.

items.title: Coherent-section quotient topologies are Fréchet and presentation-independent
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic $\mathcal O_M$-module, and let $V$ be a nonempty open subset of one holomorphic chart on which a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$ is fixed. Assume that the induced section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Then its quotient topology from compact-convergence on $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ is a Fréchet topology. If two such presentations are locally defined on a common cover and both section maps are surjective, their quotient topologies agree; the compatible-family topology on sections over any open set admitting a countable cover by such presentation neighborhoods is also Fréchet and independent of the chosen chart cover and presentations.
items.strategy: Use Artin–Rees and Krull intersection for closed relations and compare local presentation quotients.

items.title: Restriction of coherent sections to a relatively compact open set is compact
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open, and let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with compact closure contained in $\Omega$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega'$. Suppose it has a finite presentation by free sheaves on $\Omega$ and that the presentation section maps on both $\Omega$ and $\Omega'$ are surjective. Give the two section spaces the quotient topologies from compact-convergence on the finite free section spaces. Then the restriction map $\Gamma(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(\Omega',\mathcal F)$ is compact, meaning that it sends some neighborhood of zero to a set with compact closure.
items.strategy: Derive multivariable Montel compactness from Cauchy estimates, Ascoli, and a diagonal exhaustion.

items.title: Laurent decomposition of holomorphic functions on the punctured plane
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb C^*=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$. For every holomorphic function $f\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C^*)$, there are unique entire functions $g,h\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C)$ and a unique scalar $a\in\mathbb C$ such that
$$
f(z)=g(z)+a z^{-1}+z^{-2}h(1/z)\qquad(z\in\mathbb C^*).
$$
items.strategy: Extract Laurent coefficients by contour integration and prove both remaining power series entire.

items.title: Finite-dimensional coherent cohomology on compact projective space
items.statement:
Assume full AC. For $0\le r\le3$, let $P^r(\mathbb C)$ be the space of complex lines in $\mathbb C^{r+1}$ with its usual complex-manifold structure, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module over its holomorphic structure sheaf. Write $H^q(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)$ for the $q$th right-derived global-sections group. Then every such group is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$ for every integer $q\ge0$.

For its topology, a coordinate polydisc means the image in a holomorphic chart of a product of open coordinate discs. Take any finite ordered cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ by relatively compact coordinate polydiscs such that each nonempty finite intersection $U_I$ has a finite presentation $\mathcal O_{U_I}^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_{U_I}^{p_0}\to\mathcal F|_{U_I}\to0$ whose global section map is surjective, and such that $H^q(U_I,\mathcal F|_{U_I})=0$ for every $q>0$. Give $\mathcal O(U_I)^{p_0}$ compact-convergence topology and $\Gamma(U_I,\mathcal F)$ the induced quotient topology. Set $C^k(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_k}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_k},\mathcal F)$ with finite-product topology and differential
$$
(\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{k+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{k+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{k+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{k+1}}}.
$$
Give the cocycle space its subspace topology and its quotient by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. These cohomology groups are Hausdorff in that topology, which is independent of the chosen finite cover and local presentations.
items.strategy: Build a finite nested acyclic polydisc cover and apply the compact Fréchet-complex theorem.

items.title: Finite-support coherent sheaves have only finitely many sections
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $0\le r\le3$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module on $P^r(\mathbb C)$ whose support $S:=\{x\in P^r(\mathbb C):\mathcal F_x\ne0\}$ is finite. Assume each stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$, and put $\ell:=\sum_{x\in S}\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal F_x$. Then $H^0(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)\cong\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathcal F_x$ has complex dimension $\ell$, and $H^q(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$. Here $H^q$ is ordinary right-derived sheaf cohomology and $\ell$ is the total complex length of the finite-support sheaf.
items.strategy: Decompose finite-support data into skyscraper sheaves and compute their cohomology.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC and the finite-support sheaf hypotheses; no physical premise.

items.title: Compact coherent cohomology can be finite and nonzero
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $P^1(\mathbb C)$ have standard charts $U_0=\{Z_0\ne0\}$ and $U_1=\{Z_1\ne0\}$, with coordinates $z=Z_1/Z_0$ on $U_0\cong\mathbb C$ and $w=Z_0/Z_1=1/z$ on $U_1\cong\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal O(-2)$ be the projective twisting line bundle with local frames satisfying $e_1=z^{-2}e_0$ on $U_0\cap U_1\cong\mathbb C^*$. Then
$$
H^1(P^1(\mathbb C),\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C.
$$
Thus finite-dimensionality of compact coherent cohomology does not imply vanishing of positive-degree cohomology.
items.strategy: Compute the two-chart Čech quotient using the Laurent splitting on C*.
